sentences.text: Shri Surdeep Khampariya - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Mohan Sausarkar - Public Prosecutor for the State.

Order 
This is the first bail application under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 14.06.2024 in connection with Crime No.228 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Dehat, District Tikamgarh (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 343,
376(2)(N), 506 (Part-II) of the IPC.
I t is submitted that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case and has not committed any offence in any manner.
The victim is a major lady.
The victim herself has accompanied the present applicant and has travelled from one place to another.
It is submitted that victim has stayed at hotel with the present applicant with her own will.
The applicant is the first offender.
The applicant is in custody since 14.06.2024.
He is ready to abide by all terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering this bail application.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail.

P e r contra, learned counsel appearing for the State has vehemently 2 MCRC-29299-2024 opposed the prayer stating therein that there is active participation of the present applicant in the commission of offence.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the application.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the fact that the victim was major and has accompanied the present applicant without raising any hue and cry coupled with the fact that the applicant is the first offender, without commenting upon the merits of the case, this Pankaj Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37892893/

sentences.text: Court deems it appropriate to allow this application.
Accordingly, the application is allowed subject to verification of the fact that the applicant is the first offender.
He is directed to be released on bail on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.
It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the conditions as enumerated under Section 437(3) of CrPC.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
The application is accordingly allowed in above terms.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE SSL Pankaj Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37892893/
